text: Add impression-time request-context features tab, hourmin, and weekday to the neutral user/item additive scaffold while leaving the model and pointwise BCE training unchanged.
rationale: This directly tests the only feature family with positive measured screening evidence and full coverage.
exact_ablation: Ablate the request-context feature group: compare the seed's user/item IDs alone against user/item IDs plus tab, hourmin, and weekday.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected modest increase of about 0.001 to 0.004, with potentially stronger gains for cold users; the internal lift was +0.00221.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected small increase of about 0.000 to 0.003; top-five concentration may lag GAUC because cold-user nDCG@5 was 0.492 versus 0.508 for warm users/items.

text: Replace the additive logit with a factorization-machine interaction model over the existing user/item IDs and request-context features, without changing the feature set or loss.
rationale: Context signal may be conditional on user and item identity; low-rank pairwise interactions can capture that without adding screened feature families.
exact_ablation: Ablate the interaction-capable architecture: compare the additive model with a factorization-machine architecture using the same user/item and request-context inputs.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of about 0.001 to 0.004 if context effects vary by user or item; gains could disappear if the measured context lift is mostly additive.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of about 0.001 to 0.004 from improved personalization of top-ranked rows, with overfitting risk on sparse identity-context combinations.

text: Replace pointwise binary cross-entropy with within-user Bayesian Personalized Ranking loss while retaining the neutral user/item additive feature set.
rationale: The official objective is within-user ranking, so pairwise optimization is a direct loss-level alternative that does not rely on questionable feature groups.
exact_ablation: Ablate only the training loss: compare pointwise BCE against within-user BPR pair sampling using the same model inputs and architecture.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of about 0.002 to 0.008 if sampled positive-negative pairs represent users with both labels; gains may be limited by the additive model's lack of interactions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of about 0.001 to 0.006 because pairwise ordering should improve ranking, though top-five gains depend on hard-negative quality.

text: Replace pointwise BCE with a within-user listwise softmax loss over bounded user impression groups, retaining the neutral user/item additive model and avoiding unbounded all-pairs computation.
rationale: Listwise training aligns with both official ranking metrics and may concentrate probability mass on relevant items more effectively than row-wise classification.
exact_ablation: Ablate only the loss from pointwise BCE to bounded within-user listwise softmax; keep features, architecture, optimizer family, and split unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of about 0.001 to 0.006, with uncertainty from group truncation and users having few positives.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of about 0.002 to 0.008 because the loss explicitly emphasizes relative ordering within each user group.

text: Add a strictly impression-time date feature to the neutral user/item additive scaffold, leaving all other features, architecture, and training unchanged.
rationale: Date is available at ranking time and can capture temporal drift, while the request-context screen's daily lifts vary substantially across dates, including 0.00067 to 0.00913.
exact_ablation: Ablate only the date feature: compare the seed IDs-only input with IDs plus date, with no tab, hourmin, or other context fields.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected near-zero to +0.003 improvement if temporal drift is rank-relevant; it could reduce GAUC under date-specific overfitting.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected near-zero to +0.002 improvement, with weaker expected concentration than the full request-context group.

text: Add only the impression-time tab feature to the neutral user/item additive scaffold, without adding hourmin, weekday, or any other feature family.
rationale: The measured request-context result should be decomposed into interpretable single-field tests before committing the scarce official experiment.
exact_ablation: Ablate only tab: compare IDs-only against IDs plus tab, keeping model, loss, optimizer, and all other inputs unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of about 0.000 to 0.003; the full group's +0.00221 lift provides an upper-bound-like reference but does not identify tab's individual contribution.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of about 0.000 to 0.002, with uncertain top-five benefit because the screening reported stronger evidence for broad GAUC than concentration.

text: Add only the impression-time hourmin feature to the neutral user/item additive scaffold, without adding tab, weekday, or any other feature family.
rationale: Time-of-day is a plausible mechanism behind the positive request-context screen and can be tested without confounding from the other context fields.
exact_ablation: Ablate only hourmin: compare IDs-only against IDs plus hourmin, with unchanged architecture, loss, and training schedule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of about 0.000 to 0.004, potentially reflecting user-specific temporal preference variation.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of about 0.000 to 0.003; concentration may improve if time-of-day separates relevant items within users.

text: Add only the impression-time weekday feature to the neutral user/item additive scaffold, without adding tab, hourmin, or any other feature family.
rationale: Weekday is part of the positively screened request-context family and is available before the impression outcome.
exact_ablation: Ablate only weekday: compare IDs-only against IDs plus weekday, deriving weekday solely from the known impression date and changing nothing else.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of about 0.000 to 0.003, with substantial uncertainty because the aggregate screen did not isolate weekday.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected near-zero to +0.002; weekday may provide broad preference adjustment without strongly changing the top five.

text: Add the available static user-profile feature group to the neutral user/item additive scaffold while leaving architecture, loss, and training unchanged.
rationale: This is a controlled negative-check candidate: the group has full coverage but measured screening lift was -0.00054 and was recommended for rejection, so it should carry a downside-oriented expectation.
exact_ablation: Ablate only the user-profile group: compare IDs-only against IDs plus user_active_degree, lowactive status, creator flags, relationship-count ranges, and register-days range.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected near-zero to -0.003; the measured aggregate primary lift was -0.00054 and the warm-user/item GAUC was 0.629 versus 0.631 for request context.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected near-zero to -0.003, with risk that static profile biases hurt within-user item ordering despite full coverage.

text: Add only an impression-time one-hot interaction between user identity and tab to the neutral user/item additive model, retaining tab as the sole new feature family and unchanged BCE training.
rationale: The full request-context group is positive, and a user-context interaction tests whether its value comes from personalized context response rather than a global tab effect.
exact_ablation: Ablate only the user-by-tab interaction representation: compare the seed IDs-only model with the same model augmented by user-tab crossed parameters; do not add hourmin or weekday.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of about 0.000 to 0.004 for users whose tab preferences differ, but possible decline from sparse crossings.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of about 0.000 to 0.004 if tab-specific ranking is personalized; sparse users may see no gain or degradation.

text: Use hard within-user negative sampling instead of uniform negative sampling for a BPR-trained neutral user/item model, changing only the negative-sampling strategy.
rationale: Pairwise ranking is motivated by the within-user objective; hard negatives could focus updates on confusing impressions without introducing any screened or unavailable feature.
exact_ablation: Ablate only negative-sampling policy: compare uniform within-user BPR negatives with bounded hard-negative selection based on current model scores.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of about 0.001 to 0.006 if hard negatives improve ordering near the decision boundary; noisy hard negatives could reduce GAUC.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of about 0.002 to 0.007 because harder comparisons may improve top-of-list ordering, with instability risk early in training.

text: Replace the additive user/item model with a shallow two-layer MLP over concatenated user and item embeddings while keeping the IDs-only feature set and pointwise BCE unchanged.
rationale: The seed has no user-item interaction capacity; a small nonlinear architecture tests whether ranking failure is architectural without mixing in any rejected feature group.
exact_ablation: Ablate only the architecture: compare the seed additive ID model with a shallow bounded-width MLP over user and item embeddings, keeping inputs and loss fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected increase of about 0.000 to 0.005 if nonlinear user-item compatibility matters; overfitting may instead lower GAUC.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected increase of about 0.000 to 0.005, with potential top-five gains from modeling compatibility but higher variance for sparse IDs.
